metadata.adp_2024: Taken players only; no undrafted market was supplied
metadata.adp_2023: No usable ADP: the supplied 2023 export is byte-identical to the 2024 export
metadata.adp_season_validation: Each ADP column correlates highest with its own season picks (2024: 0.956, 2025: 0.913), supporting genuine season-specific markets
metadata.truncation_bias: Truncating the 2025 pool to taken-only understates mean available rank by ~12 slots and late-round reach by ~26 slots

methodology.preferences: Slot-controlled: each manager compared with the same-season league mix in the same round phase, across all three seasons
methodology.choices: Conditional logit over the ADP market available set; per-season ADP slope, preference betas shrunk toward a pooled prior
methodology.excluded: Choice sets with fewer than 12 available players are dropped (very late picks)

validation.method: Pooled 2024-25 + 2025-26 ADP choice sets; forward-round holdout + cross-season transfer
limitations: 2024-25 ADP exists only for players actually taken, so its pool is truncated: late-round reach is understated by ~26 slots. Slopes are fitted per season, never pooled across the two.
2023-24 has no usable ADP (the supplied export duplicates 2024), so it informs descriptive preferences only, never the choice likelihood.
The two ADP seasons have different pool tiers, so cross-season transfer partly reflects that difference rather than pure behavioural drift.
Positions are a 2025-26 snapshot applied to all seasons; historical position eligibility is not reconstructed.
Cross-season transfer is directional evidence, not a calibrated probability.
